See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Final score = {[(Target − Current + w × Test average) ÷ w] × (n + k) − n × Test average} ÷ k

A worked example

The current course grade is 80%, tests count 50%, and three existing tests average 70%. A final counting as one test must score 86% to reach 82% overall: the test average becomes (210 + 86) ÷ 4 = 74%, raising the course by 2 points.

Before you use the result

All existing tests must have equal weight. The final can count as several equivalent tests, while other category contributions stay fixed. The current grade must already include the test category at its full syllabus weight. Dropped tests, a separate final category or ungraded non-test work are not included.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

What does equivalent tests mean?

If the final counts twice as much as one ordinary test, enter 2. This describes relative weighting inside the test category.

Can this handle dropping the lowest test?

No. A drop changes which scores enter the category average and must be modeled separately.
